assessments.reasoning: Under the two Go 1.23 productions, an alias supplies another name for the specified type. A definition introduces its own type identity while preserving the underlying type of the right-hand side.

challenge.method: Use the same defined type T on the right of type A = T and type B T. Does the shared underlying type collapse all three identities?
challenge.results: A denotes T itself. B has a distinct identity even with the same underlying type. This conclusion requires no assumption about conversions, assignment, or experimental alias syntax.

limitations: This concerns type identity alone. It does not determine assignability, conversions, or the availability of an experimental toolchain feature.
